files.about: Every game in the Child I Fun project is built from the files in this library. Each file does one job, starts with a short header that says what it does, and can be reused in any new game.

Colors, faces, and animations for every character: the robot (worried, brave, happy, surprised, thinking faces; chest spark that grows with courage), Sunny, Rigel, Professor Kepler, flames, and the hop, walk, tremble, blink, and wag motions.
Professor Kepler, the mossy rock with tiny round glasses. Sits at (0, 0), about 52 units tall.
Nova, a teeny baby Spinosaurus with a coral sail, a long snout, and a glowing star lantern. Her outline, filled solid black and made huge, is also the giant shadow everyone calls Shadowspine.
files.provides: Kit.art.nova { SHAPES, g(options), shadow(fill), svg(options, size), url(options, size), path2d() }
files.notes:
options = { face: smile | happy | worried | surprised, lantern: true (default) | false, flip: true to face left }
Drawing space: facing right, feet at y = 0, about 62 units tall (x from -54 to 50, y from -62 to 2).
SHAPES are the outline pieces (tail, sail, body, legs, head, arm) as SVG path strings. shadow() fills them all one color,
which is how Shadowspine is drawn, and path2d() gives the same pieces for canvas drawing.

files.about: Rigel the penguin in a bubble helmet and a pink scarf. Stands at (0, 0), about 48 units tall.
Small round head portraits of the robot, Sunny, Rigel, and Professor Kepler, used in the friends bar and on helper buttons.
files.provides: Kit.art.portraits { robot, dog, peng, rock } (SVG markup strings, viewBox -16 -16 32 32)

files.about: Sunny, the fluffy magic puppy (black, white, and tan curls, floppy ears, star collar, sparkles, wagging tail). Built in code so the curls stay even. Sits at (0, 0), about 66 units tall.
files.provides: Kit.art.puppy() -> SVG markup string

files.about: The tall robot hero, side view, standing at (0, 0) and about 200 units tall. Contains every face (worried, brave, happy, surprised, thinking); characters.css picks which one shows from the robot's class and data-face. Place inside <g class="robot" id="robot">.
The robot drawn small on a canvas for walkable maps: legs swing and arms pump while walking, eyes look the way he's heading, and his chest glows brighter with courage.
files.provides: Kit.art.drawRobotTop(ctx, x, y, t, motion, { tokens, glow })
files.notes:
motion = { moving, phase, fx, fy } from kit/topdown-map.js; glow = 0 to 1 chest brightness.
tokens needs: metal, metalShade, copper, glass, snow, void, cRobot

files.about: T-Rexy, a cute cartoony green T-Rex with a big head, a big eye, two tiny teeth, and famously tiny arms. Also draws his family (same shape, different colors and accessories). Poses for standing, running, hopping, and sitting, and faces for happy, worried, surprised, thinking, dizzy, and sleepy.
files.provides: Kit.art.trexy { COLORS, g(options), svg(options, size), url(options, size) }
files.notes:
options = { pose: stand | run1 | run2 | hop | sit, face: smile | happy | worried | surprised | think | dizzy | sleepy,
            who: trexy | mom | dad | sis (colors), acc: none | flower | glasses | bow | cap, flip: true to face left }
Drawing space: facing right, feet at y = 0, about 100 units tall (x from -58 to 54, y from -94 to 2).
svg() returns a standalone <svg> (for images and canvas drawing); url() returns it as a data URL.

files.about: Shared shapes referenced with <use>: the flame (flamePath, base at 0,0, 40 units tall) and the four-point twinkle star (spark4). Place inside an inline SVG's <defs>.
Simple filled icons used on buttons so the game needs fewer words: back, go, retry, rocket, check, eye, music note, play, stop, and a shovel.
files.provides: Kit.art.icons { back, go, retry, rocket, check, eye, note, play, stop, shovel } (SVG markup strings)

files.about: Art for the top-down map of Lumina: dusty ground with craters, rocks, and glowing mushrooms, dotted paths, Comet Crater, the Old Observatory, Glowworm Grove, the Sleepy Village, the launch pad, gold star beacons with progress dots, and the glowing launch ring.
files.provides: Kit.art.luminaMap { makeDecor, drawGround, drawPaths, drawCrater, drawObservatory, drawGrove, drawVillage, drawPad, drawBeacon, drawPadRing }
files.notes:
Every draw function takes the canvas context first and a tokens object T (colors read from CSS) last.
T needs: void, gold, good, cPeng, stoneSh, metalShade, wall, roof, win, leaf, trunk, dome, scope

files.about: Four memory pictures for jigsaw puzzles, drawn in SVG: home in Fern Valley at night, the family dinner, the bedroom window at 11:11, and the swirly galaxy swoop. Each one hides a clue for the mystery if you look closely.
files.provides: Kit.art.memories { home, dinner, window, swoop } (each a function returning a standalone 400 x 300 <svg>), galaxy(cx, cy, r, turn, colors), note(x, y, scale, color)
files.notes:
Clues hidden in the pictures: a tiny glowing music box on the hill (home), a little teal tail sneaking out the door with the fish (dinner),
tiny three-toed footprints on the windowsill and a huge shadow made by a teeny moth near the lamp (window), and someone small holding
a star lantern (swoop).

files.about: Rocket motion and display: liftoff rise, hover bob, launch rumble, engine flame stretch, plus the rocket previews in the side panel (build progress, part slots, finished ship).
The buildable rocket. Data for every part choice and paint color, plus a drawing function that renders any combination (missing parts can show as dashed outlines, and one part can be highlighted).

Five neon paint jobs. Missing parts can show as dashed outlines, and a pilot can peek out of the cockpit.

files.about: The Corona Nebula scenery: a tall three-floor tower whose windows light up as data-floors goes from 1 to 3, in a 400 by 260 scene. Shows when the scene's data-world is "corona".
Planet Glacia scenery: clusters of ice spikes on both sides of a 400 by 260 scene. Shows when the scene's data-world is "glacia".

Canvas backgrounds for the Glitch Nebula: bright neon clouds, swirling galaxies, stars, a landmark for each world (a ringed planet, a fern moon, a giant lantern star, a whirlpool galaxy), and gentle glitches that nudge a stripe of the sky sideways now and then. Can also draw the giant black Shadowspine on the clouds, with an optional tiny lantern glow at its feet. Each world has its own colors for runs, too.
files.provides: Kit.art.nebula { THEMES, create() -> { draw(ctx, view, options) } }

files.about: Ground gradients for side-view worlds. Their colors come from --ground-a and --ground-b, so each world recolors them in worlds.css. Place inside an inline SVG's <defs>.

Lumina seen from the side as a small round planet that turns under the robot. Five places sit around it: launch pad (0 degrees), Comet Crater (72), Old Observatory (144), Glowworm Grove (216), Sleepy Village (288). Rotate #spin to walk between them. Windows and glowworms light up when the world is "luminaLit".
Planet Meridian scenery: carved standing stones and an old brass telescope on a tripod, in a 400 by 260 scene. Shows when the scene's data-world is "meridian".
Planet Nimbus scenery: puffy pink clouds on both sides of a 400 by 260 scene. Shows when the scene's data-world is "nimbus".
A wide curved hill for side-view planets, drawn in a 400 by 260 scene. Colored by the current world.

Colors and scenery rules for every side-view world (Lumina dark and lit, Nimbus, Glacia, Meridian, Corona): sky, ground, planet in the sky, which scenery shows, buildings, ice, stones, the tower windows, and the Everlight flame.
files.notes: Set data-world on the .scene element to switch worlds. Add .flying to drop the ground away during flights.

files.about: Assembles a game (or the library page) from its separate files into one self-contained web page, checks that every file's
files.requires: are loaded first, and writes catalog.json, the list of every file and what it does.
files.notes:
Usage, from the library folder:
  python3 build/build.py games/starward/game.json   build one game into dist/
  python3 build/build.py site/site.json            build the library page (index.html)
  python3 build/build.py --catalog                 rewrite catalog.json from the file headers
  python3 build/build.py --all                     catalog, every buildable game, then the library page

A game.json lists: title, output, fonts, styles (CSS in order), body (HTML with <!-- @include path --> lines),
scripts (shared Kit modules, assets, and content, in load order), and parts (the game's own files, which share one scope).

files.about: Automated play-test for the library: checks file headers, checks the built pages match the source, loads every page in headless Chromium at Chromebook size, and plays Starward and Mini Game Survival start to finish (every run, puzzle, flight, and secret, the ending, and the high score). Must pass before every commit that changes library/.
files.notes:
Usage, from anywhere:
  python3 library/build/playtest.py            everything (about 4 minutes)
  python3 library/build/playtest.py --quick    skip the full playthroughs
  add -v to print every screen, or --shots=DIR to save a screenshot of each Mini Game Survival screen

Needs Python 3 and Playwright. If missing:
  pip install playwright            (add --break-system-packages on Claude's workspace)
  python3 -m playwright install chromium

Checks:
  1. Headers: every source file starts with @file (its own path) and @about.
  2. Build: build.py --all, run on a copy, reproduces dist/, catalog.json, and index.html byte for byte.
  3. Pages: every built game, legacy game, and the library page load at 1366x768 with no page
     errors and no sideways scroll. Built games and the library page also allow no console errors.
     Pages are served inside the same wrapper claude.ai adds when it publishes (its base styles
     hide [hidden] elements, for example), so the test sees what Child I sees. Google Fonts is
     blocked so the run doesn't depend on outside network.
  4. Starward playthrough, with a fresh browser (so adaptive levels start at their defaults):
     - Title: name the robot and start.
     - Lumina map: walk to each place by clicking the map. The first puzzle takes three wrong
       answers; "Show me" must stay hidden until the third, then appear and reveal the answer. The second uses the Scan helper.
       Every dig must show its one-line tip, every dig is typed, every part style picked, then back to the launch pad to paint the ship.
     - Right answers: every puzzle must cheer, show no Next button, and move on by itself within 5 seconds.
     - Tapping friends: the first puzzle with Sunny on the crew is solved after tapping Sunny on the stage (her clue must
       appear), and the first with Rigel after tapping Rigel in the friends bar (a letter must appear).
     - Flights: the first try of the first flight is typed badly on purpose and must offer
       "Fly again"; every other flight is typed cleanly and must land, and the landing screen must move on by itself.
     - All planet puzzles answered, the brave words typed, and the ending reached.
     - High score: a name saves, gets a rank, and shows on the board as a score on this computer.
  5. Mini Game Survival playthrough, with a fresh browser:
     - Title, then the story lines (Enter), then the crash pad: type ROAR and poke Shadowspine (Easter eggs), click each portal.
     - Runs: the first run is left alone until T-Rexy crashes three times, which must restart him and show the
       Checkpoints button; then the built-in autopilot (the level's own solution, sped up) finishes every run and
       takes the secret route, so all four hidden diary pages must be found.
     - Jigsaws: Peek and Fix one are used on the first; every jigsaw is solved by clicking tiles.
     - Clue words: the first uses Scan after wrong letters, the second runs out of fuel and is typed to refuel.
     - Clue typing, part styles, paint, songs, the four mystery questions (one wrong answer must show a clue), the shrink, the ending.
     - After the first portal the page is reloaded, and "Keep going" must resume on the crash pad with the clue saved.
     - Right answers move on by themselves; the high score saves and the secret ending shows (all four pages).
Prints PASS or FAIL with the reasons, and exits 1 on FAIL.

files.about: Makes the shareable QR card for a game's newest release in that game's own colors and icons, with the title and version and a QR code that opens the game's permanent home page ("home" in game.json). Starward gets its night sky, gold four-point stars, and rocket; a game can set its own look with a "qr" block in game.json (Mini Game Survival: neon colors, spikes, jigsaw pieces, and T-Rexy's head). Checks that the finished card scans back to the right link.
files.requires: kit/base.css, assets/fx/defs.svg, assets/icons/icons.js, assets/characters/trexy.js (colors and icon shapes are copied from these)
files.notes:
Usage, from the library folder:
  python3 build/qr.py games/starward/game.json     card for the newest release in game.json
Writes dist/<id>-v<N>-qr.png. Needs Pillow and opencv-python-headless (pip install opencv-python-headless).
Uses the qrcode package when installed (pip install "qrcode[pil]"); otherwise OpenCV's own QR encoder makes the code.
Exits 1 if the card does not scan back to the release link.

Optional "qr" block in game.json:
  { "colors": { void, nebula, nebulaHi, starlight, dust, glow, accent, gold, onGold }, "badge": "star" | "trexy", "cta": "Scan to play!" }

files.about: Building blocks for obstacle runs: short stretches of spikes, steps, bounce pads, gaps, ship tunnels, and one secret stretch with a hidden box up high. A run is put together from these, easier ones at low levels and trickier ones at high levels.
files.provides: Kit.levels.runner (list of chunks)
files.notes:
Format is described in kit/runner.js. min and max are the run levels (1 to 5) a chunk can appear at, w is how often it is picked.
Every chunk starts with at least 2 tiles of flat ground. The hero's hop is tiny (about 1.25 tiles), so two spikes in a row
or anything 2 tiles high needs a bounce pad. The level generator plays each chunk with its solver before using it.
tag "ship" = a ship tunnel (between a ship portal S and a hero portal C). tag "secret" = holds the hidden box x, reached by
hopping onto a thin ledge with a pad on it; running straight under the ledge is the normal way through.

files.about: 46 fill-in-the-blank sentences about space, robots, and science for ages 8 to 10, each tagged easy (1), medium (2), or hard (3). ___ marks the blank.
files.provides: Kit.questions.banks.blanks

files.about: 21 Earth and geography questions (continents, oceans, mountains, deserts, famous places), each tagged easy (1), medium (2), or hard (3).
files.provides: Kit.questions.banks.earth

files.about: Math question generators that make new problems every time: space word problems, missing numbers, place value, rounding, and number patterns. Each takes a level from 1 to 5. Level 1 is early second grade, 3 is third grade, 5 is fourth grade.
files.provides: Kit.questions.gens { word, missing, place, round, pattern }
files.notes:
Number ranges by level:
  add       1: 1-10        2: 10-60      3: 100-450     4: 150-900     5: 1,000-5,000
  subtract  1: within 20   2: within 100 3: within 1,000 (bigger gaps at 4) 5: within 10,000
  multiply  1: x2, x5, x10 2: up to 5x5  3: up to 9x9   4: 1 digit x 2 digits   5: 2 digits x 2 digits
  divide    matches multiply (always comes out even)

files.about: Generator for "which one does not belong?" puzzles: three things from one group and one sneaky outsider. Level 1 mixes very different groups (tools and planets); level 3 is trickier (the Moon among planets).
files.provides: Kit.questions.gens.odd

files.about: Generator for planet-order questions. Level 1 asks about Earth's neighbors, level 2 about any planet, level 3 asks "which planet is fifth from the Sun?"
files.provides: Kit.questions.gens.order, Kit.questions.PLANETS

files.about: 36 STEM-leaning riddles for ages 8 to 10, each tagged easy (1), medium (2), or hard (3). The clue is what a helper friend says when asked.
files.provides: Kit.questions.banks.riddles

files.about: 48 science and space words to unscramble, from 4 to 7 letters. Longer words are harder, so games choose the length from the player's level.
files.provides: Kit.questions.banks.scramble (each item has len)

files.about: 17 space riddles (planets, stars, comets, rovers), each tagged easy (1), medium (2), or hard (3). Each has two clues: one for a sniff hint and one for a ponder hint.
files.provides: Kit.questions.banks.space

files.about: Science words with kid-friendly hints for word-guessing games, in four topics: sound and music, food and dinosaurs, light and shadows, and space. Each word is tagged easy (1), medium (2), or hard (3).
files.provides: Kit.words.clues { sound, food, light, space } each a list of [WORD, difficulty, hint]
files.notes:
Easy words are 4 or 5 letters, medium 5 to 7, hard 6 to 11. Hints never use the word itself. No word appears in two topics,
so one game never asks the same word twice.

files.about: Word lists for typing practice, sorted by length: short words, five-letter words, longer words, short phrases, cozy "home" words, and digging words.
files.provides: Kit.words { short, five, long, phrases, home, dig }

files.about: The first game: a tall, scared robot types his way across four planets, solves riddles, and makes friends (a magic puppy, a penguin, and a mossy rock) on the way to the flame that relights his world. Kept as one legacy file; its characters, music style, and question ideas live on in the library as Starward's modules.
Original single-file source, kept unchanged so this version can always be rebuilt or edited.

Starts Mini Game Survival: connects each story step type to its screen, resumes saved games (rebuilding the scene from the story so far), turns on Enter-to-continue, and keeps the game going through live page updates.

Mini Game Survival's neon look: hot pink, laser cyan, and glitch yellow colors on a deep purple night, a glitchy title, the wide scene during runs, the jigsaw board over the scene, the clue notebook and secret diary pages, the run buttons, the mystery choices, and the part and paint pickers.

T-Rexy, a cute little T-Rex with a tiny jump, wakes up alone in the glitchy neon Glitch Nebula after weird music swoops him away from home. He runs four obstacle portals (bounce pads, ship tunnels, spikes), rebuilds his memories in jigsaw puzzles, spells science clue words before the glitch drains his fuel, types each clue into his notebook, and builds a spaceship to get home. Then he solves the mystery of Shadowspine, the giant all-black Spinosaurus. Hidden diary pages and other secrets, hardcore music, adaptive difficulty, and an arcade high score board.

Mini Game Survival's page layout: the top bar (ship parts, clues, music and sound), the scene window (one canvas for the hub, the runs, and story scenes, plus the jigsaw board, the run buttons, the countdown, and the high score board on the title screen), and the side panel.

Everything Mini Game Survival draws in the scene window: story scenes (T-Rexy's faces and hops, Shadowspine on the clouds, Nova, the ship, the family), the walkable crash pad with its portals and Easter eggs (poke Shadowspine, type ROAR, tiny footprints, a hidden glitch message), and the obstacle runs. Also the music, the toggles, the top bar, and toasts.

files.about: Starward's story, in order: every line, every world change, every friend, puzzle, flight, and song. To change the story, edit this list. Step types: world, say, appear, join, explore, build, puzzle, song, fly, flame, end.
Adaptive difficulty. Tracks how the player is doing in each skill and moves that skill's level up or down. Levels are remembered on that computer for that game.
files.provides: Kit.adaptive.create({ key, skills, onChange }) -> { level(skill), record(skill, outcome), adjust(skill, delta), snapshot() }
files.notes:
skills: { name: { min, max, start } }, for example { math: { min: 1, max: 5, start: 3 } }
record(skill, outcome) rules:
  "clean"    solved on the first try with no hints. Two in a row: level up.
  "ok"       solved after one miss or with a hint. Level stays the same.
  "struggle" solved after two or more misses. Two in a row: level down.
  "gaveup"   needed "Show me". Level down right away.
adjust(skill, +1 or -1) changes a level directly (typing rounds use this).
onChange(skill, newLevel, delta) runs whenever a level actually changes.

files.about: Sound effects made in code (no audio files): beeps, chimes, whooshes, a woof. Also unlocks sound on the first click or key press, which browsers require.
files.provides: Kit.audio { ctx, noiseBuffer, tone, noise, sfx, enabled, setEnabled, onFirstGesture }

files.about: Core look shared by every game: color and font tokens, the one-screen layout (top bar, scene, side panel), buttons, text boxes, choice tiles, title text, and toasts. Single dark space theme by design.
Tiny canvas drawing shortcuts used by map art and top-down characters: circles, ovals, rounded boxes, glows, stars, and fog holes.
files.provides: Kit.draw { circle, ellipse, rr, glow, star4, hole }

files.about: The speed-typing round: words fall like shooting stars and must be typed before they reach the bottom. Missed words are not retyped. Also the 3, 2, 1, Liftoff countdown and the accuracy goal bar.
files.provides: Kit.flight { run(options) -> stop, countdown(options) -> Promise<boolean>, goalBar(pct, id, goal), starRow(n, results) }
files.notes:
run options:
  arena      element the words fall through (position: absolute; inset: 0)
  panel      element for the typing display
  head       HTML shown at the top of the panel
  words      list of words or short phrases, in order
  timing     { base, per, slow }: seconds to fall = (base + per * letters) * slow
  maxFalling how many words can be on screen at once (default 2)
  alive()    returns false once the player has left this screen
  onCatch()  called when a word is finished (for effects)
  onEnd(result) result = { hits, misses, caught, n, typeMs, typeChars, acc, res }

files.about: Runs a game's story as a list of steps (say a line, show a puzzle, fly, and so on). Each step type has a handler. Also holds the cleanup for whatever screen is showing, so leaving a screen always stops its timers and key listeners.
files.provides: Kit.flow.create({ steps, handlers, beforeStep }) -> { go, next, step, token, alive, bump, setCleanup, cleanupNow, replay }
files.notes:
A handler returns true when its step is instant (change world, add a friend); the flow then moves straight to the next step.
token() and alive(t) let slow actions (countdowns, walks) check they still belong to the current screen.
replay(upto, { type: fn }) re-applies instant steps when resuming a saved game.

files.about: Styles for the letter-guessing game: the hint, the secret word's letter boxes, the fuel tank cells (they flicker when zapped), and the on-screen letter keys.

A friendly letter-guessing game (no hangman): a secret word, a riddle-style hint, and a fuel tank. Type or tap letters to guess. Right letters light up in the word; each wrong letter drains one fuel cell. If the fuel runs out, the word is shown and the player types it to refuel and keep going, so nobody gets stuck.
files.provides: Kit.fuelWord.render(panel, options) -> { use(key) }
files.notes:
options = { head (HTML), tip (one short line), word, hint, fuel (number of cells), cheers, autoNext (ms, default 1700),
            scanAfter (wrong letters before the Scan helper pulses, default 2), helperHtml (icon for the Scan button),
            onGuess(letter, ok), onScan(), onOut(), onWin({ misses, scans, out, fuelLeft, cheer }), onDone() }
use("scan") presses the Scan helper from outside the panel (for example, tapping the hero); it reveals one letter, once.

files.about: Styles for the picture jigsaw: the tile grid, the selected tile, tiles that are home (locked with a glow), the peek overlay, and the solved picture.

Picture jigsaw: a picture is cut into a grid of tiles and shuffled. Swap two tiles to fix it. Works with arrow keys and Enter, or by clicking two tiles. Tiles that are home lock in place with a glow. Helpers can peek at the whole picture or put one tile home.
files.provides: Kit.jigsaw.render(board, options) -> { peek(), fix(), stop(), placed(), total }
files.notes:
options = { svg (a standalone <svg> string), rows, cols, label, onMove(placed, total), onDone({ moves, best, peeks, fixes }) }
best = the fewest swaps that could have solved it, so a game can score how close the player came.

files.about: Styles for the jukebox song list and the "New song!" title.
A list of collected songs with play and stop buttons. Songs not found yet show as locked.
files.provides: Kit.jukebox.render(el, { order, songs, owned, where, music, icons, onTurnOn, fallback })
files.notes:
order     song ids in display order
songs     Kit.songs (each has a title)
owned()   ids the player has collected; the first id in order is always owned
where(id) where the song is found, shown under its title
music     the player made by Kit.music.create
icons     { note, play, stop } HTML
onTurnOn  called if pressing play had to switch music back on
fallback  song id to return to when a playing song is stopped (default: the first in order)

files.about: Plays looping background songs that are written as data and synthesized in code (no audio files, nothing copyrighted).
files.provides: Kit.music.create(songs) -> { set(id), unlock(), setEnabled(on), enabled, want }
files.notes:
Song format (see assets/music/*.js):
  title     name shown in jukeboxes
  bpm       tempo; each step is an eighth note
  root      MIDI note number of the key (60 = middle C)
  lead      32 steps: semitones above root, or null for a rest
  chords    4 chords (one per 8 steps), each a list of semitone offsets
  bass      8 steps: 1 = chord root, 2 = root an octave up, 0 = rest
  kick, hat 8 steps of 1 or 0 (optional drums)
  optional: wave, oct, pluck, leadVol, leadLen, pad, padWave, bassWave, bassVol, bassLen, hatVol

files.about: Styles for the puzzle screen: question kind tag, fill-in blank, letter tiles, helper buttons, clues, and right or wrong feedback (a big popping cheer for a right answer).
Shows one question with an answer box, helper buttons, and feedback. Works with every question kind in kit/questions.js (riddles, fill in the blank, scrambles, number patterns, odd one out, math).
files.provides: Kit.puzzleUI { render(panel, question, options) -> { use(helperKey) }, blankHTML }
files.notes:
options:
  head        HTML above the question (place name, progress dots)
  leave       function for a "walk away" back button (optional)
  helpers     [{ key, type: "scan" | "clue" | "peek" | "clue2", label, iconHtml, color, who, onUse }] in display order
              scan = show how many letters; clue = show question.clue; peek = reveal a letter; clue2 = show question.clue2
  icons       { check, eye, back } HTML
  autoNext    ms to show the cheer after a right answer before moving on by itself (default 1700; a shown spelling or answer adds 900).
              0 shows a Next button instead.
  nextHtml    HTML for that Next button (only used when autoNext is 0)
  cheers      cheers to pick from after a right answer (default: a few general ones)
  showAfter   wrong answers before "Show me" appears (default 3)
  onHint(type), onWrong(tries), onNudge(helperKey), onWin({ shown, tries, hints, spell, cheer }), onDone()

render returns { use(key) }: presses a helper from outside the panel (for example, tapping a friend
on the stage). It returns true if the helper was used, false if it is used up, hidden, or the puzzle is gone.

files.about: The question system: banks of written questions, generators that make new ones on the fly, a picker that matches the player's level and avoids repeats across games, and the answer checker.
files.provides: Kit.questions { addBank, banks, gens, KIND, createPicker, judge, scrambled }

files.about: Side-scrolling obstacle run, like a rhythm platformer: the hero runs by himself, hops over spikes, bounces off pads, and flies a little ship through tunnels. Touching a spike or a wall sends him back to the start (or the last checkpoint, once checkpoints are on). Levels are built from chunks, and a built-in solver plays every chunk before it is used, so every level can be beaten.
files.provides: Kit.runner { sim: { DT, PHYS, Level, start, step, clone, solve }, generate(options), play(canvas, options) -> { stop, pause(on), checkpoints(on), state } }

files.about: Arcade look for the high score board, the name entry box, and the end-of-game score card.
Arcade-style high score board. Uses the page's shared database when it's available and falls back to scores saved on this computer. Draws into every element marked data-scoreboard.
files.provides: Kit.scoreboard.create({ storeKey, collection, size }) -> { init(), render(), save(entry) -> rank, all() }
files.notes:
The published page must declare capabilities: { db: {} } for the shared board.
Entry shape: { name, score, at (ISO date), ...any extra fields }

files.about: A walkable side-view home area. The hero walks left and right with the arrow keys or A and D, or walks to wherever you click. Stops along the way (like portals) can be entered with Enter, Space, or the up arrow, or by clicking them. The game draws everything; this module handles walking, the camera, clicks, and typed secret words.
files.provides: Kit.sidehub.create(canvas, options) -> { stop(), hero, view(), walkTo(x, enterId), setStops(stops), say(text, ms) }

files.about: A twinkling starfield on a canvas that can streak into warp speed during flights.
files.provides: Kit.starfield.create(canvas, { color, count }) -> { boost(), warp(on), pause(on) }

files.about: A walkable top-down map on a canvas. The player moves with arrow keys, WASD, or by clicking; walking into a place triggers it. Includes fog with light holes, particle bursts, speech bubbles, and an arrow-key hint until the player first moves.
files.provides: Kit.topdownMap.create(options) -> map { start(pos), stop(), on, busy, pos, say(text, ms), burst(x, y, color, n), stepOutOf(site) }
files.notes:
options:
  canvas, width, height       map size in map units (the canvas scales to fit)
  speed, enterRadius          walking speed (units per second) and how close counts as "arrived"
  bounds                      { minX, maxX, minY, maxY } where the player can walk
  sites                       [{ id, x, y }] places that trigger onArrive
  drawWorld(c, t)             draw ground and places (map units)
  drawPlayer(c, x, y, t, m)   draw the player; m = { moving, phase, fx, fy }
  drawAbove(c, t)             draw things that sit above the fog (beacons)
  fog                         { rgb: "r,g,b", alpha(), holes(pos) -> [{ x, y, r, a }] } (optional)
  onArrive(site), onMove(), showHint() -> boolean
  colors                      { light, dark } for bubbles and the arrow-key hint
  font                        font family for speech bubbles

files.about: Two untimed typing challenges. dig: type the words written on clumps of dirt to dig something up. line: type one sentence exactly (like a brave promise).
files.provides: Kit.typing { dig(panel, options) -> stop, line(panel, options) -> stop }

files.about: Styles for typing challenges: falling word chips, the countdown, the big word display, the accuracy goal bar, the caught-star row, and the dirt clumps for digging.
Shared screen helpers: the main Next button, progress dots, toasts, focus, Enter-to-continue, and reading theme colors for canvas drawing.
files.provides: Kit.ui { reduced, focusSoon, bindPrimary, nextBtn, pips, toaster, enterAdvances, tokens, blurActive }

files.about: Small helpers every game uses: finding elements, random picks, answer matching, and safe browser storage.
files.provides: Kit.util { $, wait, shuffle, sample, pick, rint, clamp, esc, norm, squash, lev, cleanName, store }

files.about: Look of the Game Library page: light and dark themes, game cards with version lists, the flow map, night-sky character tiles, the song list, and the file browser.
Layout of the Game Library page: games and versions, how the pieces fit, live characters, rocket, and ship, songs, the file browser, and how to change a game later.

Fills in the Game Library page from catalog.json: games and their versions, the flow map, the live robot, T-Rexy, Nova, rocket, and ship previews, the song player, and the file browser that can show any file's source.
files.requires: kit/util.js, kit/audio.js, kit/music.js, assets/icons/icons.js, assets/characters/puppy.js, assets/rocket/rocket.js, assets/characters/trexy.js, assets/characters/nova.js, assets/ship/glitch-ship.js

files.about: Build list for the Game Library page itself: it reuses the same characters, rocket, ship, music, and engines as the games so they can be previewed live.

games.title: The Inner Flame
games.about: The first game: a tall, scared robot types his way across four planets, solves riddles, and makes friends (a magic puppy, a penguin, and a mossy rock) on the way to the flame that relights his world. Kept as one legacy file; its characters, music style, and question ideas live on in the library as Starward's modules.

releases.notes: Original game, designed by Child I by voice.

games.title: Mini Game Survival v1
games.about: T-Rexy, a cute little T-Rex with a tiny jump, wakes up alone in the glitchy neon Glitch Nebula after weird music swoops him away from home. He runs four obstacle portals (bounce pads, ship tunnels, spikes), rebuilds his memories in jigsaw puzzles, spells science clue words before the glitch drains his fuel, types each clue into his notebook, and builds a spaceship to get home. Then he solves the mystery of Shadowspine, the giant all-black Spinosaurus. Hidden diary pages and other secrets, hardcore music, adaptive difficulty, and an arcade high score board.

games.title: Starward v6
games.about: A tall robot, the Keeper of Lumina, explores his dark home world to rebuild his rocket, then flies to four planets with new friends to bring back the Everlight. Typing flights, STEM puzzles, collectible songs, adaptive difficulty, and an arcade high score board.

releases.notes: First Starward: new names and story, rocket parts on Lumina, falling-word flights, fill-in-the-blank puzzles, songs, high scores. Kept in that page's version history (version 1 of the page).
Walkable Lumina map, three challenges per rocket part, fresh questions every game, fewer instructions. Current version of that page. Single-file source: games/starward/legacy/v3.html
Rebuilt from the library. Adaptive difficulty for typing, math, and word puzzles; questions chosen to match the player's level.

Same game as v4 with no personal names: the title screen says "An original space adventure". The first version on the permanent home page, whose high scores now carry across updates. Archived to its own page on 2026-10-17 when v6 shipped.

One-line tip on every Lumina dig; a big cheer after a right answer, then the game moves on by itself (no Next button); safe landings and the brave words move on by themselves; tap Sunny on the stage or in the friends bar to sniff for a clue (Rigel peeks, Professor Kepler ponders).
